subject: Edge mini-cluster: capacity, IO SLAs & heterogeneous node plan
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novapulse.com
Date: 2028-12-20T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial intake: compact edge cluster requirements and SLA questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We're moving forward with a 3-site pilot of NovaPulse's inference appliances and need Redwood Private installed into a compact on-prem footprint at each site. High-level asks:

- Target throughput: 75 tokens/s sustained per site (inference baseline for 3x concurrent models).
- P95 latency target: <= 180ms for 512-token prompts.
- Storage: local cache for KV/LLM checkpoints with persistent blockstore backup.
- Data retention & encryption: at-rest encrypted (customer KMS), retention 90 days, audit logs retained 1 year.

We attached our capacity template and a small sample of NVMe perf tests from lab. Can you confirm node mix recommendations (GPU counts, local NVMe sizing vs remote blockstore), network egress expectations, and any constraints for a compact (single-rack) deployment?

Also, what fallback behaviour do you recommend if local NVMe becomes saturated?

Appreciate a sketch of node-pool and storage layout so I can share with our infra team for approval.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Cloud Ops Lead, NovaPulse
attachments: novapulse_capacity_template.xlsx; nvme_perf_samples.tar.gz
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-12-21T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: compact edge cluster requirements and SLA questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the detail and the test artifacts. Quick ack and a short plan below; Karthik will follow up with the technical matrix for node sizing.

High-level recommendations (for a single-rack compact footprint):

- Heterogeneous node pool approach: 2x GPU inference nodes (A-pool), 2x mixed CPU+small-gpu batching nodes (B-pool), 1x control+ops node (C-pool). This balances latency and throughput while keeping power/cooling predictable.
- Local storage: each inference node should have 2 x 3.84TB NVMe (RAID1-like mirror at app level or software mirror) for KV cache and checkpoints. This supports fast local KV access and reduces remote reads.
- Persistent blockstore: replicated block device (NFS/SMB or iSCSI-backed cloud-block equivalent provided by customer) for model artifacts and long-term checkpoints. Mount read-only on inference nodes, writable from control node for uploads.
- Eviction/fallback: enable prefix/KV cache eviction policy + transparent streaming to blockstore. If NVMe saturation detected, requests fall back to smaller-batch execution path (degraded throughput) and stream missing KV segments from blockstore — add an automatic circuit-breaker to route to a lower-capacity model variant when load is sustained.
- Network: 25GbE minimum on inference nodes; prefer separate management VLAN for control plane and KV/blockstore traffic. Egress: plan for 300Mbps spike per site for model pulls and telemetry.

I'll attach a short checklist and capacity sketch. Karthik — can you produce a concise node-sizing matrix (GPU model options, expected tokens/s at P50/P95, recommended NVMe capacity per GPU) so we can align on SLA feasibility?

Next steps:
1) Karthik to send sizing matrix by 12/23.
2) We iterate model variant fallback policies and caching thresholds.
3) Draft a minimal runbook for NVMe saturation scenarios.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: compact_footprint_sketch.pdf (attached)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com; Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>
Date: 2028-12-22T14:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: compact edge cluster requirements and SLA questions

Kimberly / Alice — attached is the node-sizing matrix (summary below). I focused on a realistic mid-range GPU (A100-40GB equivalent) and a lower-power T4-like node for batching.

Summary (per site):
- A-pool (2 nodes): 1 x A100-40 equiv / node, expected sustained 80 tokens/s per node at 512 tokens (single-stream, optimized kernel), P95 ~ 150ms. NVMe: 3.2TB usable per node for KV + local model cache.
- B-pool (2 nodes): 2 x CPU-heavy boxes with 1 small inference GPU (T4-like) or large CPU for batching; used for burst consolidation and background scoring. NVMe: 1.6TB per node.
- C-pool (1 node): 2x vCPU-equivalent for control plane + blockstore gateway; 500GB for logs and model staging.

Storage design notes:
- Use local NVMe for KV cache and model shard hot storage. Checkpoint sync to blockstore every 5 minutes (configurable).
- Blockstore should expose a POSIX interface (NFSv4.2 recommended) with 3-way replication across the customer's infra for resilience. Mount with read-mostly semantics on inference nodes.
- Encryption: integrate with customer's KMS (KMIP or cloud KMS via VPN) — store keys and handle rotation at control plane.

Fallback & SLOs:
- If local NVMe I/O > 85% sustained for 30s, trigger: (1) reduce batch size; (2) fall back to B-pool batching path; (3) degrade to smaller model variant after 2 min sustained high I/O while emitting alert.
- Circuit breaker publishes events to Ops with severity.

Operational:
- Recommend on-site monitoring (Prom + node-exporter + NVMe SMART alerts) with remote alert forwarding to NovaPulse PagerDuty.
- Runbook includes steps to evacuate a node (drain, migrate KV warm cache from peer, rehydrate from blockstore).

I'll attach the sizing table and quick perf curves. If we need to support GPUs with <40GB memory, quantization and per-shard placement strategies need to be added to the plan.

-Karthik
attachments: node_sizing_matrix.csv (attached); perf_curves.png (attached)
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novapulse.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-12-24T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: compact edge cluster requirements and SLA questions

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule an infra approval meeting:

1) For the A-pool NVMe sizing you recommend ~3.2TB usable. Our hardware BOM has 3.84TB devices; is that acceptable as-is or do you prefer larger?
2) On blockstore replication: our internal team prefers 2-way synchronous + async offsite replication. Will Redwood rely on POSIX semantics or do you need stronger coherency guarantees?
3) Can we get an initial draft of the runbook steps you mentioned (evacuate/drain/rehydrate) — even a 1-page play is fine for approvals.

Also attaching the filled capacity template with environment details. If everything looks good, we'll book a 45-min approval call next week (Jan 2) with our infra and security leads.

Best,
Alice
attachments: novapulse_capacity_template_filled.xlsx

- Neha: validate the KMS integration options and confirm whether KMIP or vendor KMS is required.

I'll join the Jan 2 meeting and bring the deployment checklist.

-Marissa
Senior Delivery Manager, Redwood Inference
